comparisons.peer_topic: Operating cash flow and drivers in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Net cash provided by operating activities was $3 billion in 2024, primarily driven by net income of $1.6 billion, non-cash adjustments of $3.5 billion, and net cash outflows of $2.1 billion from changes in operating assets and liabilities, including a $1.9 billion increase in accounts receivable due to higher year-end revenue and a $1.5 billion increase in inventories to support new product ramps.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze the primary drivers of 2024 cash flow from operations. Intel reports negative $2.2 billion in adjusted free cash flow and $8.3 billion in cash from operations, impacted by significant non-cash charges and restructuring, whereas AMD reports positive $3 billion in net cash from operating activities, driven by net income and non-cash adjustments but offset by working capital outflows for receivables and inventory.

sentences.text: In 2024, we invested $16.5 billion in R&D, made gross capital investments of $25.1 billion, and had $8.3 billion in cash from operations and negative $2.2 billion of adjusted free cash flow [footnote 1: See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" within MD&A.] .

Net cash provided by operating activities was $3 billion in 2024, primarily due to our net income of $1.6 billion in 2024, adjusted for non-cash adjustments of $3.5 billion and net cash outflows of $2.1 billion from changes in our operating assets and liabilities.

The primary drivers of the changes in operating assets and liabilities included a $1.9 billion increase in accounts receivable driven primarily by higher revenue in the last month of 2024 compared to the last month of 2023, and a $1.5 billion increase in inventories driven primarily by a build of inventory to support the ramp of new products in advanced process nodes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Deferred tax asset valuation allowance policy
comparisons.peer_summary: A valuation allowance is recorded for deferred tax assets unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not; conversely, if realization is deemed more-likely-than-not, existing valuation allowances may be reversed, resulting in a credit to income tax expense.
comparisons.comparison: Intel's 2024 results included non-cash charges for a valuation allowance against US deferred tax assets as a specific financial impact on consolidated results. AMD's disclosure details the general policy for recording or reversing valuation allowances on deferred tax assets based on the 'more-likely-than-not' threshold for recovery, highlighting the shared technical topic of deferred tax asset realizability assessments, though AMD focuses on the accounting policy rather than a specific 2024 charge impact.

sentences.text: Our consolidated results of operations in 2024 were meaningfully impacted by non-cash impairments and the acceleration of depreciation for certain manufacturing assets, restructuring charges resulting from our 2024 Restructuring Plan, non-cash impairments of goodwill and certain other assets, as well as non-cash charges related to a valuation allowance recognized against our US deferred tax assets.

Unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not (a probability level of more than 50%), we will record a charge to income tax expense in the form of a valuation allowance for the deferred tax assets that we estimate will not ultimately be recoverable or maintain the valuation allowance recorded in prior periods.

When considering all available evidence, if we determine it is more-likely-than-not we will realize our deferred tax assets, we will reverse some or all of the existing valuation allowance, which would result in a credit to income tax expense and the establishment of an asset in the period of reversal.

comparisons.peer_topic: Cash flow from operating activities change due to VMware
comparisons.peer_summary: Cash provided by operations increased by $1,877 million in fiscal year 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to contributions from VMware, despite an $8,187 million decrease in net income largely driven by $13,058 million higher non-cash adjustments related to the VMware Merger.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss cash flow from operations in 2024, specifically addressing the relationship between net income and cash provided by operations. Intel notes consolidated results were meaningfully impacted by non-cash charges (impairments, depreciation, valuation allowance) alongside restructuring charges. Broadcom highlights that despite an $8,187 million decrease in net income, cash provided by operations increased, driven by VMware contributions and $13,058 million in higher non-cash adjustments (amortization, stock-based comp, deferred taxes).

sentences.text: Our consolidated results of operations in 2024 were meaningfully impacted by non-cash impairments and the acceleration of depreciation for certain manufacturing assets, restructuring charges resulting from our 2024 Restructuring Plan, non-cash impairments of goodwill and certain other assets, as well as non-cash charges related to a valuation allowance recognized against our US deferred tax assets.
The $1,877 million increase in cash provided by operations during fiscal year 2024 compared to fiscal year 2023 was primarily due to contributions from VMware.

The $8,187 million decrease in net income was largely driven by $13,058 million higher non-cash adjustments including amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation, and deferred taxes and other non-cash taxes related to the VMware Merger.

Broadcom explicitly lists 'restructuring charges' as a component included in its total cost of revenue. Both identify restructuring charges as a relevant financial line item in their 2024 financial reporting, though Intel frames it as an operating result impact while Broadcom frames it as a cost of revenue component.

sentences.text: Our consolidated results of operations in 2024 were meaningfully impacted by non-cash impairments and the acceleration of depreciation for certain manufacturing assets, restructuring charges resulting from our 2024 Restructuring Plan, non-cash impairments of goodwill and certain other assets, as well as non-cash charges related to a valuation allowance recognized against our US deferred tax assets.
Total cost of revenue also includes amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets and restructuring charges.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, cash provided by operating activities increased compared to 2023, primarily driven by net income adjusted for non-cash items, increases in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities (largely due to customer prepayments), partially offset by an increase in receivables.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures detail the drivers of operating cash flow. Intel provides specific 2024 metrics: $8.3 billion cash from operations and negative $2.2 billion adjusted free cash flow, impacted by large non-cash charges. Micron provides a comparative year-over-year analysis for 2024 vs 2023, noting cash provided by operating activities increased due to net income adjusted for non-cash items, partially offset by increases in receivables, while highlighting the significance of non-cash adjustments in their cash flow reconciliation.

sentences.text: In 2024, we invested $16.5 billion in R&D, made gross capital investments of $25.1 billion, and had $8.3 billion in cash from operations and negative $2.2 billion of adjusted free cash flow [footnote 1: See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" within MD&A.] .

The increase in cash provided by operating activities for 2024 as compared to 2023 was primarily due to net income in 2024 adjusted for non-cash items, the effect of an increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses and an increase in other current liabilities largely due to customer prepayments to secure product supply, partially offset by an increase in receivables.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation allowance for deferred tax assets
comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, the company maintained valuation allowances of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, related to capital loss carryforwards and certain state and other deferred tax assets determined not likely to be realized. If realization becomes more-likely-than-not, such deferred tax assets would be recognized as income tax benefits during the period.
comparisons.comparison: Intel reports that its 2024 consolidated results were impacted by 'non-cash charges related to a valuation allowance recognized against our US deferred tax assets.' NVDA discloses maintaining a $1.6 billion valuation allowance against deferred tax assets (capital loss carryforwards and state assets) as of the end of fiscal 2024, determining they were 'not likely to be realized.' Both disclosures identify valuation allowances for deferred tax assets as a material financial consideration in 2024.

sentences.text: Our consolidated results of operations in 2024 were meaningfully impacted by non-cash impairments and the acceleration of depreciation for certain manufacturing assets, restructuring charges resulting from our 2024 Restructuring Plan, non-cash impairments of goodwill and certain other assets, as well as non-cash charges related to a valuation allowance recognized against our US deferred tax assets.

As of the end of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, we had a valuation allowance of $1.6 billion and $1.5 billion, respectively, related to capital loss carryforwards, and certain state and other deferred tax assets that management determined are not likely to be realized due, in part, to jurisdictional projections of future taxable income, including capital gains.

comparisons.peer_topic: Capital investment funding expectations for fiscal 2025
comparisons.peer_summary: For fiscal year 2025, the company expects to use existing cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities, and operating cash flows to fund capital investments of approximately $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion related to property and equipment.
comparisons.comparison: Intel reports gross capital investments of $25.1 billion and R&D investment of $16.5 billion in 2024, indicating massive capital deployment. NVDA discusses its expectations for funding capital investments ($3.5-$4.0 billion) for fiscal 2025 using existing cash and operating flows. Both companies address the magnitude and funding of capital investments, though Intel reports historical 2024 spend while NVDA provides forward-looking 2025 funding expectations, differing significantly in scale and timing.

sentences.text: In 2024, we invested $16.5 billion in R&D, made gross capital investments of $25.1 billion, and had $8.3 billion in cash from operations and negative $2.2 billion of adjusted free cash flow [footnote 1: See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" within MD&A.] .

During fiscal year 2025, we expect to use our existing cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, and the cash generated by our operations to fund our capital investments of approximately $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion related to property and equipment.
